If you think your nvidia card runs too hot, you can take control of fan speed pretty easily.

First of all, you need to set Bit 2 of Coolbits to enable manual fan speed control. Add 

Option "Coolbits" "4"

to your xorg.conf in Section "Device".

Now you can use following command

nvidia-settings -a [gpu:0]/GPUFanControlState=1 -a [fan:0]/GPUTargetFanSpeed=40

to set any speed in percentage.

Add following script to your autostart and it will take care of the rest. Of course, you can fiddle with values to get optimal settings for your video card.

#!/bin/sh

interval=10 # run script each $interval seconds
safe_temp=40 # if temperature <= $safe_temp set fan speed to $normal_speed
normal_speed=50 # default fan speed
plus_speed=10 # offset value to calculate needed fan speed

while true; do
 current_temp=`nvidia-settings -t -q [GPU:0]/GPUCoreTemp`
 if [ "$current_temp" -le $safe_temp ]; then
 nvidia-settings -a [gpu:0]/GPUFanControlState=1 -a [fan:0]/GPUTargetFanSpeed=$normal_speed
 else
 speed=$(( $plus_speed + $current_temp ))
 if [ "$speed" -gt 100 ]; then speed=100; fi
 nvidia-settings -a [gpu:0]/GPUFanControlState=1 -a [fan:0]/GPUTargetFanSpeed=$speed
 fi
 sleep "$interval"
done
[TIP] Simple script to control your video card's fan speed (nvidia)
